item.text: I’ll check the sanitizer’s state handling, make a local fix in that implementation, then run the specified test and stop.

I found the two paths behind the failures: a closing marker can advance the index to the line’s end and still reach byte access, and marker detection currently runs inside ordinary strings. I’ll make triple-quote handling consume its own bytes and only start it outside a regular quote.

Fixed the Python sanitizer so a triple-quote marker at a line boundary is consumed safely and a marker inside an ordinary string does not start a multiline string. Other language handling was left unchanged.
